question.worked_solution:
Recall that by definition, $\text{nullity}(C)=\text{dim}(\text{Null}(D)).$

To find $\text{dim}(\text{Null}(C))$, we reduce $C$ to row echelon form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}C & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -2 & -1 \\ 0 & 3 & -1 & -4 \\ 3 & -6 & -4 & 5\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-3){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -2 & -1 \\ 0 & 3 & -1 & -4 \\ 0 & -6 & 2 & 8\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+2{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -2 & -1 \\ 0 & 3 & -1 & -4 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix has $2$ pivot columns and $2$ non-pivot columns (namely, the $3$rd and $4$th columns). 

Therefore,

$$
\text{nullity}(C)=\text{dim}(\text{Null}(C))=2.
$$
